title: Test Check-in — Gale St (Rock Springs)
description: Dev/test quest at 347 Gale St, Rock Springs WY. Easy check-in to verify GPS + photo + OLC claim. Safe to complete.

title: Hell's Revenge Trailhead
description: Hell's Revenge is a Moab slickrock trail on BLM land east of the Colorado River, famous for steep off-camber fins and the Hot Tub drop. Sandstone grippiness when dry made it a proving ground for locked, high-clearance builds. Check current regulations — this is technical terrain, not a scenic cruise.

title: Elephant Hill Trailhead
description: Elephant Hill is the gateway to Canyonlands' Needles District backcountry, notorious for steep rock steps that demand short-wheelbase skill. Beyond the hill, jointed Cedar Mesa sandstone creates one of the Southwest's great jeep and hike landscapes. Permits and high clearance are essential.

title: Burr Trail Switchbacks
description: The Burr Trail began as a cattle route built by rancher John Atlantic Burr across what is now Grand Staircase–Escalante and Capitol Reef country. Steep switchbacks drop off the Waterpocket Fold into Strike Valley. Graded dirt and pavement mix depending on the segment — views are enormous.

title: Notch Peak Trailhead
description: Notch Peak in Utah's House Range hosts one of North America's highest pure limestone cliffs, rising above West Desert valleys. Remote BLM roads reach trailheads used by climbers and peakbaggers. The isolation explains why this skyline remains quiet compared with Zion or Arches.

title: Little Sahara Sand Dunes
description: Little Sahara Recreation Area protects a Jurassic sandstone dune field on BLM land in central Utah's Sevier Desert. Wind piles free sand into riding hills popular with OHVs and sandboards. Oasis campground cottonwoods mark a surprising green spot in the basin.

title: Paiute ATV Trail (Circleville)
description: The Paiute ATV Trail system links hundreds of miles of multi-use routes across Fishlake National Forest and adjoining public lands. Circleville is a classic southern Utah access community. High-plateau forests and desert edges alternate along the network.

title: Mingus Mountain Forest Road
description: Mingus Mountain rises between Prescott and Jerome with ponderosa roads and overlooks toward the Verde Valley. Mining and railroad history thread the Black Hills of Arizona. Cooler air makes it a summer escape from desert heat.

title: Canyon de Chelly Overlook Road
description: Canyon de Chelly National Monument protects continuous Navajo (Diné) homeland and Ancestral Puebloan cliff dwellings in sheer red sandstone canyons. South Rim overlooks including Spider Rock interpret living culture and deep archaeology. Tribal guides lead canyon-floor tours.

title: Lake Havasu Backcountry
description: Lake Havasu's desert tracks explore Mohave County country above the Colorado River reservoir created by Parker Dam. London Bridge's relocation made the town famous; the backcountry remains hot, rocky, and remote. Carry abundant water.

title: Death Valley Dunes (Mesquite)
description: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes are Death Valley's most accessible dune field, sculpted by winds trapped near the Grapevine Mountains. Crescent and star dune forms shift seasonally. They sit far below sea-level-adjacent basins that define the valley's extremes.

title: Racetrack Playa Road
description: Racetrack Playa is home to sailing stones that leave tracks across a dry lake — moved by rare ice-window winds, not mystery alone. The rough washboard road from Ubehebe Crater demands high clearance and full-size spare tires. Night skies here are pristine.

title: Titus Canyon Road
description: Titus Canyon's one-way drive through the Grapevine Mountains passes lead-mining ruins at Leadfield and narrow limestone walls. It is among Death Valley's premier scenic geology routes. Check flood and road-status reports before committing.

title: Kīlauea Overlook — Hawaiʻi Volcanoes
description: Kīlauea is one of the world's most active volcanoes and the heart of Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park. This rim overlook faces Halemaʻumaʻu crater, where Pele traditions and modern eruption science meet. Steam plumes and occasional glow explain why this summit landscape is sacred and closely monitored.

title: Punaluʻu Black Sand Beach
description: Punaluʻu's black sand is basalt pulverized by Kaʻū coast surf. Green and hawksbill turtles haul out on warm sand beneath palms. It is a classic circled-island stop and a reminder that new land here is only centuries old.

title: ʻAkaka Falls State Park
description: ʻAkaka Falls plunges 442 feet through Hāmākua rainforest northeast of Hilo. A paved loop also passes Kahuna Falls among ʻōhiʻa and tropical plantings. The park protects one of the Big Island's most photographed waterfalls.

title: Waipiʻo Valley Lookout
description: Waipiʻo — Valley of the Kings — was a political and spiritual center for early Hawaiian aliʻi. The lookout frames cliffs, black sand, and taro fields fed by ancient stream systems. The steep valley road is 4WD-only and often restricted.

title: Puʻukoholā Heiau National Historic Site
description: Kamehameha I built this massive stone heiau in 1790–91 after a prophecy tied it to conquest of the islands. The temple overlooks Kawaihae Bay and ranks among Hawaiʻi's best-preserved royal heiau. It marks a turning point toward the unified kingdom.

title: Waiʻānapanapa State Park
description: Waiʻānapanapa offers black sand, sea caves, a blowhole, and a coastal trail past cultural sites. Legends of Princess Popoʻalaea are tied to the freshwater caves inland. It is East Maui's signature stop before Hāna.

title: ʻIao Valley State Monument
description: ʻIao Needle rises above a West Maui stream valley where Kamehameha defeated Maui forces in the 1790 Battle of Kepaniwai. The park interprets the battle and botanical gardens along the walkway. It is a compact window into Maui's unification era.

title: Waimea Canyon Lookout
description: Waimea Canyon cuts ~10 miles long and ~3,000 feet deep into weathered Kauaʻi basalt — the Grand Canyon of the Pacific. Red walls and hanging valleys record millions of years of erosion on the island's oldest shield. Kōkeʻe Road pullouts deliver classic views.

title: Spouting Horn Park
description: Spouting Horn is a lava-tube blowhole on Kauaʻi's south shore that shoots spray with a deep moan. Nearby remnants recall 19th-century salt-making and shipping. It remains one of Poʻipū's most accessible geologic spectacles.

title: Diamond Head (Lēʻahi) Trailhead
description: Lēʻahi is a tuff cone formed ~200,000 years ago and later fortified for Oʻahu coastal defense. The trail climbs through a military tunnel to a bunker-lined summit over Honolulu. It is both a volcanic landmark and early 20th-century Pacific strategy.

title: Kaʻena Point Approach — Mokuleʻia
description: Kaʻena is Oʻahu's westernmost tip — dunes, tidepools, and albatross nesting habitat. Tradition places a leaping-off point for souls here. Unpaved coastal access demands care within the natural area reserve.

title: South Point (Ka Lae) Approach
description: Ka Lae is the southernmost point of the United States and a National Historic Landmark of early Polynesian landfall. Mooring holes and heiau remnants speak to centuries of fishing and navigation. Windswept cliffs feel like the edge of the map.

title: Kealakekua Bay Overlook
description: Kealakekua Bay is where Captain Cook was killed in 1779 after first being received during makahiki. A white obelisk marks the far shore from Nāpōʻopoʻo. Steep cliffs frame one of Hawaiʻi's most consequential contact-history landscapes.

title: Lava Tree State Monument
description: Lava Tree preserves molds formed when 1790 pahoehoe surged through a wet ʻōhiʻa forest and chilled around trunks. The resulting stone 'trees' record a moment of Kīlauea's east rift history. A short loop explains the process in place.

title: Kalaupapa Overlook — Molokaʻi
description: From the pali overlook above Kalaupapa, cliffs drop nearly 2,000 feet to the isolation settlement peninsula. Hansen's disease patients were exiled here beginning in 1866; Father Damien and Mother Marianne Cope are central to its story. The view alone conveys the site's gravity.

title: Hālawa Valley Lookout — Molokaʻi
description: Hālawa is one of Molokaʻi's most storied valleys, with ancient taro loʻi and twin coastal waterfalls. Tsunami and cultural change reshaped settlement, but the amphitheater remains iconic. The lookout sits at the east end of Highway 450.

title: Puʻu Pehe (Sweetheart Rock) Overlook
description: Puʻu Pehe is a sea stack off Lānaʻi's Hulopoʻe–Mānele coast tied to a tragic love legend. Trails from Mānele offer views of the islet and marine preserve waters. It is Lānaʻi's signature coastal landmark.

title: Exit Glacier — Kenai Fjords
description: Exit Glacier is one of the most accessible tidewater-region glaciers in Kenai Fjords National Park. Rapid retreat here has become a public timeline of climate change, with dated signs marking former ice edges. The valley walk shows raw moraine and outwash left behind.

title: Independence Mine State Historical Park
description: Independence Mine was a major hard-rock gold operation in the Hatcher Pass district above Palmer. Boardwalks and mill ruins interpret the 1930s–50s boom that drew miners into the Talkeetna Mountains. The alpine setting is as striking as the industrial archaeology.

title: Worthington Glacier Recreation Site
description: Worthington Glacier spills toward the Richardson Highway east of Thompson Pass. It is one of Alaska's roadside glaciers, with short trails to viewpoints over blue ice and debris bands. Thompson Pass itself is legendary for extreme snowfall.

title: Eagle River Nature Center Trailhead
description: The nature center anchors Chugach State Park access up Eagle River Valley near Anchorage. Trails interpret boreal forest, salmon streams, and occasional moose or bear sign. It is a classic urban-wildland gateway for Southcentral Alaska.

title: Denali Viewpoint South — Parks Highway
description: Clear-day pullouts on the Parks Highway frame Denali, North America's highest peak at 20,310 feet. Athabascan peoples have long known the mountain as Denali — the High One. Roadside views here rival many in-park vistas when weather cooperates.

title: Chena Hot Springs Road End Area
description: Chena Hot Springs has drawn Interior Alaska travelers for over a century to granite country northeast of Fairbanks. Natural mineral waters and aurora-season tourism define the modern resort. The long road in is a classic Interior overland spur.

title: Arctic Circle Wayside — Dalton Highway
description: This Dalton Highway wayside marks 66°33′N, where continuous daylight or darkness can occur. The haul road was built for the Trans-Alaska Pipeline in the 1970s. Reaching it is a badge of Interior and North Slope overlanding.

title: Finger Mountain Wayside — Dalton Hwy
description: Finger Mountain's granite tor rises above tundra along the Dalton south of the Arctic Circle. Pullouts interpret alpine-arctic botany and pipeline history. It is a landmark on the lonely haul to Deadhorse.

title: Crow Creek Mine Road — Girdwood
description: Crow Creek was one of Southcentral Alaska's productive placer creeks during the Turnagain Arm gold rush. A historic mine site still offers panning demonstrations in summer. The dirt road climbs into Chugach forest above Girdwood.

title: Cape Flattery Trailhead
description: Cape Flattery is the northwesternmost point of the contiguous U.S., on Makah lands. Boardwalks lead to cliffs overlooking Tatoosh Island and wild Pacific swells. Makah cultural history and treaty rights are central to understanding this cape.

title: Cape Disappointment Lighthouse Area
description: Cape Disappointment marks the mouth of the Columbia where Lewis and Clark reached the Pacific in 1805. Lighthouses and coastal defense batteries later guarded the bar known as the Graveyard of the Pacific. Cliffs and driftwood beaches complete a storied landfall.

title: Palouse Falls State Park
description: Palouse Falls drops ~200 feet into a basalt canyon carved by Ice Age Missoula Floods. It is Washington's official state waterfall and a dramatic channeled-scablands landmark. Overlooks explain megaflood geology in plain view.

title: Smith Rock State Park — Misery Ridge TH
description: Smith Rock's welded tuff cliffs helped birth modern American sport climbing. The Crooked River bends below spires that draw climbers and hikers year-round. Ranching history and state park protection share the canyon.

title: Fort Rock State Natural Area
description: Fort Rock is a tuff ring rising from Oregon's high desert, with nearby Fort Rock Cave yielding some of the oldest footwear in the world. The circular cliffs once stood in a pluvial lake. It is a landmark of Northern Great Basin prehistory.

title: Shoshone Falls Overlook
description: Shoshone Falls on the Snake River drops higher than Niagara in a basalt canyon at Twin Falls. Irrigation-era diversion and hydropower shaped modern Magic Valley agriculture. Overlooks explain why settlers called it the Niagara of the West.

title: Craters of the Moon — Loop Road
description: Craters of the Moon preserves a vast lava field on the Great Rift with cinder cones and tubes. Apollo astronauts trained here for lunar geology. The loop road samples pahoehoe, āā, and spaterry vents in a compact volcanic park.

title: City of Rocks National Reserve
description: City of Rocks' granite domes guided California Trail emigrants who wrote axle grease graffiti on Register Rock. Today it is a premier climbing reserve with pioneer wagon traces. Silent City formations still look like a skyline of towers.

title: Glacier Point — Yosemite
description: Glacier Point overlooks Half Dome, Vernal and Nevada Falls, and the Yosemite Valley floor from 3,200 feet above. It became a carriage-road spectacle in the late 1800s and remains a defining Sierra viewpoint. Granite cliffs record ice-age sculpting of the range.

title: Badwater Basin Salt Flats
description: Badwater Basin at 282 feet below sea level is the lowest point in North America. Salt polygons form as Death Valley's ephemeral lake evaporates. The stark flats explain the valley's name better than any plaque.

title: Torrey Pines Gliderport Overlook
description: Bluffs above Black's Beach host rare Torrey pines and a historic gliderport with Pacific panoramas. The reserve protects the mainland's rarest pine species against coastal development pressure. Hang gliders and migrating whales share the skyline.

title: Point Reyes Lighthouse Area
description: Point Reyes Lighthouse was built in 1870 on a windy tip notorious for fog and shipwrecks. Steps descend to the lantern room overlooking elephant seal beaches and open ocean. The peninsula's granite is an exotic terrane rafted north along the San Andreas.

title: Morro Rock — Morro Bay
description: Morro Rock is a 576-foot volcanic plug — the 'Gibraltar of the Pacific' — sacred to Chumash peoples and a navigational landmark for Spanish mariners. Quarrying scars remain from harbor work. Peregrine falcons nest on its cliffs.

title: Burney Falls — McArthur-Burney
description: Burney Falls drops ~129 feet as an unexpectedly wide curtain fed by underground springs as well as surface flow. Theodore Roosevelt reportedly called it one of America's wonders. Basalt cliffs and evergreen forest frame the mist.

title: Napa Sonoma State Historic Parks Hub — Sonoma Barracks
description: Sonoma Barracks and the plaza were central to Mexico's northern frontier and the short-lived 1846 Bear Flag Revolt. Adobe buildings still face the town square. The site anchors California's transition from Mexican Alta California to U.S. statehood.

title: Cathedral Gorge State Park
description: Cathedral Gorge's soft bentonite badlands erode into slot-like corridors and spires in Nevada's eastern desert. CCC structures and a slot canyon walk highlight Depression-era park building. It is a quiet geologic gem near Panaca.

title: Sand Mountain Recreation Area
description: Sand Mountain is a singing dune complex beside Highway 50 — the Loneliest Road in America. OHV play and desert camping draw weekend crowds to the 600-foot dune. The sand sheet is a remnant of Ice Age Lake Lahontan shore processes.

title: Wupatki Pueblo Overlook
description: Wupatki was a multi-story pueblo that flourished after the Sunset Crater eruption enriched soils. Trade goods from the Pacific and Mesoamerica show far-reaching networks. The red sandstone complex sits between Flagstaff and the Little Colorado.

title: Four Corners Monument
description: Four Corners is the only point in the U.S. shared by four states — Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, and Utah — on Navajo and Ute Mountain Ute lands. The survey monument is a modern geopolitical curiosity on ancestral lands. Visitors typically stand in four states at once.

title: Calf Creek Falls Trailhead
description: Lower Calf Creek Falls drops 126 feet into a green oasis along the Escalante River corridor. Fremont pictographs and beaver wetlands share the canyon. The trailhead sits on Scenic Byway 12 between Boulder and Escalante.

title: Snow Canyon State Park
description: Snow Canyon mixes Navajo Sandstone cliffs with black basalt flows near St. George. Ancestral Puebloan and Paiute histories precede Mormon pioneer use of the canyon. Scenic drives and trails sample petrified dunes and lava tubes.

title: Antelope Island — Bridger Bay Area
description: Antelope Island is the Great Salt Lake's largest island, home to bison and pronghorn on lacustrine benches. Causeway access reveals the lake's salinity and bird-rich shores. Fielding Garr Ranch interprets early settlement on the island.

title: Trail Ridge Road — Rock Cut Area
description: Trail Ridge Road is the highest continuous paved highway in the U.S., cresting above 12,000 feet in Rocky Mountain National Park. Rock Cut viewpoints open onto alpine tundra that feels Arctic. Ute and Arapaho peoples crossed these high routes long before auto tourism.

title: Garden of the Gods — North Gateway
description: Garden of the Gods' vertical Fountain Formation fins rise against Pikes Peak on ancestral Ute lands. Railroad magnate Charles Elliott Perkins's family gifted the park for free public access. Balanced rock and Kissing Camels are classic Front Range icons.

title: Royal Gorge Bridge Park
description: The Royal Gorge Bridge (1929) spans the Arkansas River more than 950 feet above the water. Once the world's highest suspension bridge, it remains a Front Range–Arkansas River tourism landmark. Steep gondolas and Via Ferrata routes add modern adventure layers.

title: Florissant Fossil Beds Visitor Center
description: Florissant preserves Eocene lakebed fossils — enormous petrified stumps and delicate insects — in volcanic ash shales. 19th-century collectors and later conservation battles shaped the monument. Quiet meadows sit beneath Pikes Peak country.

title: Pompeys Pillar National Monument
description: Pompeys Pillar bears William Clark's 1806 signature — the only remaining physical evidence of Lewis and Clark along their route. The sandstone bluff overlooks the Yellowstone River. Crow and earlier peoples left older petroglyphs on the rock.

title: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument
description: Little Bighorn marks the 1876 battle where Lakota, Northern Cheyenne, and Arapaho warriors defeated Lt. Col. Custer's battalion. Markers across the ridges interpret both U.S. Army and Indigenous perspectives. It remains one of the most consequential sites of the Plains wars.

title: Makoshika State Park — Cap Rock Area
description: Makoshika — 'bad earth' or 'badlands' in Lakota — is Montana's largest state park, with dinosaur fossils in Hell Creek Formation exposures. Cap rocks protect softer sediments into hoodoos near Glendive. Sunrise paints the badlands orange and lavender.

title: Petroglyph National Monument — Rinconada Canyon
description: Tens of thousands of petroglyphs were pecked into Albuquerque's West Mesa basalt by Ancestral Puebloans and later Spanish settlers. Rinconada Canyon trails pass dense panels with volcanic vistas. Urban trails meet deep time on the city's edge.

title: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
description: Enchanted Rock is a pink granite batholith dome sacred to Tonkawa and other peoples and a landmark for Spanish and Anglo travelers. Exfoliation slabs and vernal pools crown the summit. It is Central Texas's classic pluton hike.

title: San Antonio Missions — Mission San José
description: Mission San José y San Miguel de Aguayo — Queen of the Missions — anchored Spain's frontier evangelical and farming complex along the San Antonio River. UNESCO-listed missions tell Indigenous and colonial stories together. The rose window is an architectural icon.

title: Cape Blanco / Texas Coast — Mustang Island SP
description: Mustang Island State Park protects Gulf barrier-island dunes and beach south of Port Aransas. Whooping cranes winter nearby in Aransas NWR across the bay. Wind, surf, and coastal prairie define South Texas overlanding near the water.

title: Jewel Cave National Monument
description: Jewel Cave is one of the world's longest caves, lined with calcite crystals that inspired its name. Discovery and exploration stories stretch from 1900 into modern survey pushes. It sits in ponderosa forest of the Black Hills.

title: Wind Cave National Park Visitor Area
description: Wind Cave features rare boxwork calcite formations and is sacred in Lakota emergence tradition. Above ground, one of the country's largest remaining mixed-grass prairies supports bison. Barometric 'breathing' at the entrance gave the cave its name.

title: Theodore Roosevelt NP — North Unit Overlook
description: The North Unit's River Bend overlooks frame Little Missouri badlands that shaped Theodore Roosevelt's conservation ethic after hunting and ranching here. Painted Canyon hues and cottonwood bottoms define western North Dakota. Elk and longhorn are often visible.

title: Sleeping Bear Dunes — Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive
description: Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore towers above Lake Michigan with perched dunes and an Anishinaabe origin legend of a mother bear and cubs. Pierce Stocking Drive delivers overlooks from forest to inland lakes. Bluff edges show how wind and ice sheets remade the coast.

title: Isle Royale — Rock Harbor Visitor Area
description: Isle Royale is a roadless Lake Superior wilderness island famous for wolf–moose dynamics and ancient copper mining. Rock Harbor is the primary ferry and lodge gateway. Getting here is an expedition by boat or seaplane.

title: Effigy Mounds National Monument
description: Effigy Mounds protects American Indian burial and ceremonial mounds shaped like animals along the Mississippi River bluffs. Woodland cultures built them over a thousand years ago. Trails interpret sacred landscapes still meaningful to descendant nations.

title: Gateway Arch National Park
description: Eero Saarinen's Gateway Arch (1965) commemorates St. Louis as the gateway to westward expansion. The underground museum revisits Lewis and Clark, Dred Scott, and river-city history. The 630-foot stainless span defines the Mississippi skyline.

title: Hot Springs National Park Bathhouse Row
description: Bathhouse Row preserves Gilded Age spas built on protected thermal springs claimed as America's first federal reserve (1832). The park sits inside a working city. Quapaw and later spa culture made the valley a healing destination.

title: Mammoth Cave Historic Entrance Area
description: Mammoth Cave is the world's longest known cave system, with exploration still extending maps through limestone labyrinths. Enslaved guides were central to 19th-century tourism stories. The historic entrance area anchors a UNESCO World Heritage park.

title: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
description: Cumberland Gap was the natural notch through the Appalachians used by Indigenous peoples and later Daniel Boone's Wilderness Road. Thousands of settlers poured west through this pass. Pinnacle Overlook surveys three states.

title: Chickamauga & Chattanooga — Point Park
description: Point Park on Lookout Mountain commemorates the Civil War Battles for Chattanooga above the Tennessee River bend. Ochs Museum and batteries overlook the Moccasin Bend. It is among the earliest U.S. military parks.

title: Natchez Trace Parkway — Double Arch Bridge Area
description: The Natchez Trace follows a historic Indigenous and frontier route from Nashville toward Natchez. Near Birdsong Hollow, a modern double-arch bridge frames the parkway aesthetic. Mileposts interpret stands, inns, and boatmen's walks.

title: New Orleans — Jackson Square & St. Louis Cathedral
description: Jackson Square was the Plaza de Armas of French and Spanish colonial New Orleans, facing St. Louis Cathedral. The Cabildo and Presbytère frame Louisiana Purchase history. Street musicians keep the square a living Creole stage.

title: Everglades — Anhinga Trail Boardwalk
description: The Anhinga Trail offers close views of alligators, anhingas, and sawgrass marsh at the Everglades' edge. It interprets a wetland ecosystem unique in North America. Water management and restoration debates define the park's modern mission.

title: Dry Tortugas — Fort Jefferson Ferry Landing Area
description: Fort Jefferson is a massive Third System brick fort on Garden Key, 70 miles west of Key West. It held Civil War prisoners and later became a national park with living coral. Reaching it by ferry or seaplane is part of the quest.

title: Castillo de San Marcos National Monument
description: Castillo de San Marcos is the oldest masonry fort in the continental U.S., built by Spain beginning in 1672 to defend St. Augustine. Coquina walls absorbed British cannon fire. It anchors continuous European settlement history in Florida.

title: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex Area
description: The visitor complex interprets Cape Canaveral and Kennedy Space Center launches that sent Americans to orbit and the Moon. Saturn V exhibits and pads across the Banana River tell Cold War and STEM stories. Coastal wildlife refuges surround the spaceport.

title: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
description: Harpers Ferry sits at the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah where John Brown's 1859 raid accelerated the path to Civil War. Armory ruins and steep streets pack layers of American conflict and industry. Appalachian Trail hikers pass through town.

title: Assateague Island — Verrazzano Bridge Approach Area
description: Assateague is famous for wild horses descended from domestic stock on a barrier island shared by Maryland and Virginia. Dunes, marshes, and ocean beach shift constantly. Storm overwash continually rewrites the map.

title: Gettysburg National Military Park — Visitor Center Area
description: Gettysburg was the Civil War's pivotal July 1863 battle and the site of Lincoln's Gettysburg Address. Ridge lines and farm lanes remain readable landscapes of the three-day fight. It is among the most studied battlefields on Earth.

title: Independence National Historical Park — Liberty Bell Center
description: The Liberty Bell and Independence Hall anchor the founding documents of the United States in Philadelphia. UNESCO-listed buildings interpret revolution, slavery's contradictions, and constitutional debate. Old City streets retain 18th-century fabric.

title: Cape May Lighthouse
description: Cape May Light (1859) guides ships past the cape at Delaware Bay's mouth, tip of a Victorian seaside city. Migratory birds pour through in spectacular seasons. The lighthouse sits in a state park amid dunes and gun batteries.

title: Statue of Liberty / Liberty Island Ferry Approach Views
description: Liberty Enlightening the World (1886) became the defining immigrant welcome in New York Harbor. Bartholdi's statue and Bartholdi–Eiffel engineering sit on Fort Wood's star base. Ellis Island nearby completes the immigration story.

title: Niagara Falls — Prospect Point
description: Prospect Point overlooks the American Falls and Bridal Veil where the Niagara River plunges into a gorge toward Ontario. Hydroelectric history and honeymoon tourism shaped the border cities. Mist and thunder define one of North America's great waterfalls.

title: Acadia — Cadillac Mountain Summit
description: Cadillac Mountain is the highest point on the U.S. Atlantic coast and among the first sites of sunrise in winter. Carriage roads and granite summits define Acadia National Park on Mount Desert Island. Glacial polish and pink granite are classic Acadia.

title: Cape Cod National Seashore — Marconi Beach Area
description: Marconi Beach honors Guglielmo Marconi's 1903 transatlantic wireless station on Outer Cape Cod. National Seashore dunes and wave-cut cliffs show relentless Atlantic erosion. The Outer Cape remains a literary and ecological icon.

title: Minute Man National Historical Park — North Bridge
description: The North Bridge in Concord is where colonial militia engaged British regulars on April 19, 1775 — Emerson's 'shot heard round the world.' Battle Road traces the fighting toward Boston. Stone walls and farms preserve a revolutionary landscape.

title: Newport Cliff Walk — The Breakers Access Area
description: Newport's Cliff Walk threads between Gilded Age mansions and rocky Atlantic shore. The Breakers and neighbors display Vanderbilt-era wealth. Public right-of-way along the cliffs is a hard-won Rhode Island tradition.

title: Mystic Seaport Museum Waterfront
description: Mystic Seaport preserves a working 19th-century maritime village with the Charles W. Morgan whaleship. Connecticut's seafaring economy built ports that traded globally. Demonstrations keep wooden-boat skills alive.

title: Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park
description: This Woodstock estate interprets conservation history from George Perkins Marsh through Billings and Rockefeller stewardship. Carriage roads climb Mount Tom above the Ottauquechee Valley. It is a cradle narrative of American environmental thought.

title: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse Area
description: Cape Hatteras Light is the tallest brick lighthouse in the U.S., guarding Diamond Shoals — the Graveyard of the Atlantic. It was moved inland in 1999 to escape erosion. Barrier-island dynamics constantly threaten and remake the Outer Banks.

title: Wright Brothers National Memorial
description: Here Wilbur and Orville Wright achieved controlled powered flight on December 17, 1903, over Kill Devil Hills dunes. Monuments mark flight paths on the Outer Banks. Steady winds and soft sand made the site ideal for experiments.

title: Congaree National Park — Boardwalk Loop
description: Congaree protects old-growth bottomland hardwood forest with some of the tallest trees in the eastern U.S. Elevated boardwalks cross floodplain that feels primeval. It is a rare remnant of a once-vast southeastern ecosystem.

title: Fort Sumter National Monument Ferry Landing
description: Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor is where the Civil War's first shots were fired in April 1861. The island fort's brick ruins interpret the siege that opened four years of conflict. Ferries leave from Liberty Square and Patriots Point.

title: Okefenokee — Suwannee Canal Recreation Area
description: Okefenokee is one of North America's largest blackwater swamp wildernesses, headwaters of the Suwannee River. Boardwalks and boats explore peat prairies and cypress. Seminole and earlier peoples knew its labyrinth long before park status.

title: Cumberland Island National Seashore Dock Area
description: Cumberland Island mixes wild beaches, feral horses, and Carnegie-era ruins reachable mainly by ferry. Dungeness mansion remnants speak to Gilded Age retreats. It is Georgia's largest barrier island preserve.

title: Little River Canyon National Preserve
description: Little River flows for most of its length atop Lookout Mountain before plunging into one of the deepest canyon systems in the East. Rim drives and falls overlooks feel unexpectedly western. Sandstone cliffs shelter rare plants.

title: Vicksburg National Military Park
description: Vicksburg's 1863 siege gave the Union control of the Mississippi River — a turning point of the Civil War. Monuments crown ridges above the river bends. USS Cairo's recovered ironclad is a rare surviving gunboat.

title: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
description: Tallgrass Prairie preserves a remnant of the ecosystem that once covered much of the Great Plains. Flint Hills ranching continues beside restored prairie and a historic ranch headquarters. Bison graze where homesteaders met endless grass.

title: Scotts Bluff National Monument
description: Scotts Bluff was a landmark on the Oregon, California, and Mormon Pioneer trails rising above the North Platte Valley. Wagon ruts and summit views interpret the great overland migration. Mitchell Pass funneled emigrants west.

title: Chimney Rock National Historic Site
description: Chimney Rock's spire was the most noted landmark of the Oregon Trail, recorded in countless emigrant diaries. Soft Brule clay continues to erode the spire's height. It signaled the approach to the Rockies for wagon companies.

title: Homestead National Historical Park
description: Homestead interprets the 1862 Homestead Act that transferred vast public lands to private farms — reshaping Indigenous homelands and the Plains. Tallgrass restoration surrounds the heritage center. It is the flagship site for that land-policy story.

title: Fort Laramie National Historic Site
description: Fort Laramie was the pivotal trading post and military fort of the Northern Plains overland trails. Treaties signed here attempted — and often failed — to manage conflict on Indigenous lands. Restored buildings sit at the Laramie and North Platte confluence.

title: Legend Rock Petroglyph Site
description: Legend Rock hosts hundreds of Indigenous petroglyphs on sandstone cliffs in the Bighorn Basin. Panels span millennia of Plains visual culture. Remote BLM/state management aims to protect fragile rock art.

title: Fossil Butte National Monument
description: Fossil Butte preserves Eocene Fossil Lake fishes and plants in paper-thin limestone — some of the world's finest fossils. The visitor center displays extraordinary complete specimens. Quiet high desert surrounds Kemmerer country.

title: Moraine Lake Rockpile Viewpoint
description: Moraine Lake sits in the Valley of the Ten Peaks, once featured on Canadian currency. The rockpile viewpoint frames Wenkchemna Peaks above impossibly blue water. Access is timed in peak season to protect the fragile corridor.

title: Banff — Surprise Corner Viewpoint
description: Surprise Corner overlooks the Banff Springs Hotel and Bow River falls area — a classic Canadian Pacific Railway tourism tableau. Hot springs discovery in the 1880s led to Banff becoming Canada's first national park. Cascade Mountain anchors the skyline.

title: Icefields Parkway — Bow Lake Num-Ti-Jah Area
description: Bow Lake mirrors Crowfoot Glacier along the Icefields Parkway, one of the world's great mountain drives. Num-Ti-Jah Lodge recalls early guide Jimmy Simpson's era. The parkway links Banff and Jasper through continuous rock and ice.

title: Miette Hot Springs Area
description: Miette Hot Springs are the hottest in the Canadian Rockies, flowing from limestone on Jasper's east side. A historic aquacourt tradition continues with mountain views. Elk often graze the approach road meadows.

title: Yoho — Emerald Lake Lodge Area
description: Emerald Lake's vivid color sits beneath the President Range in Yoho National Park. A circuit trail and historic lodge recall early CPR tourism. The Burgess Shale quarries nearby revolutionized understanding of Cambrian life.

title: Glacier NP Canada — Rogers Pass Discovery Centre
description: Rogers Pass was the CPR's snowbound ordeal through the Selkirks, later tamed by the Connaught and Mount Macdonald tunnels and avalanche defenses. The discovery centre interprets railway sacrifice and mountain weather. Today's Highway 1 still closes for controlled slides.

title: Kootenay — Radium Hot Springs Pools Area
description: Radium Hot Springs sit at the southwestern gate of Kootenay National Park in a rocky canyon of the Kootenay River. Aquacourt tradition dates to early park tourism. Iron-rich water leaves a mineral tint.

title: Pacific Rim — Long Beach Breaker Area
description: Long Beach in Pacific Rim National Park Reserve is a vast surf-pounded strand on Vancouver Island's west coast. Nuu-chah-nulth territories encompass these shores. Fog, cedars, and Pacific swell define the Rainforest Coast.

title: Cathedral Grove — MacMillan Provincial Park
description: Cathedral Grove protects monumental Douglas-fir and cedar stands along Highway 4 to Port Alberni. Some trees are centuries old — a remnant of coastal old growth. Boardwalks try to balance access and root protection.

title: Hope Slide Viewpoint
description: The 1965 Hope Slide buried Highway 3 under millions of tonnes of rock, killing four motorists. A viewpoint interprets the scar still visible on the mountainside. It is a sobering lesson in Fraser Valley geology.

title: Fort Langley National Historic Site
description: Fort Langley was a Hudson's Bay Company depot and the site where British Columbia was proclaimed a crown colony in 1858. Reconstructed palisades interpret fur-trade life on the Fraser. It anchors the Lower Mainland's colonial origin story.

title: Harrison Hot Springs Waterfront
description: Harrison Hot Springs has been a mineral-soak destination since the 19th century at the south end of Harrison Lake. Mountains rise directly from the lake into the Coast Range. Sts'ailes and other nations' histories precede resort development.

title: Muncho Lake Provincial Park — Strawberry Flats
description: Muncho Lake's jade waters sit along the Alaska Highway amid the northern Rockies. Folded mountains plunge toward one of BC's most beautiful roadside lakes. It is a landmark of the long drive toward Yukon.

title: Liard River Hot Springs Provincial Park
description: Liard Hot Springs are a lush warm oasis on the Alaska Highway where boreal forest meets tropical-feeling boards through warm swamps. Moose sometimes wade the warm outlets. It is the classic soak for northbound travelers.

title: Sign Post Forest — Watson Lake
description: Watson Lake's Sign Post Forest began in 1942 when a homesick GI put up a sign pointing toward his hometown during Alaska Highway construction. Tens of thousands of signs now cover the grove. It is roadside folk culture of the North.

title: Yukon — Emerald Lake Viewpoint
description: Emerald Lake south of Whitehorse glows from marl (calcium carbonate) reflecting in shallow water. It is a quick scenic stop on the South Klondike Highway toward Skagway. Mountains frame a color that seems unreal.

title: White Pass Summit — Klondike Highway
description: White Pass was a brutal gold-rush gateway from Skagway toward the Yukon interior, later crossed by the White Pass & Yukon Route railway. The highway summit still feels alpine and windswept. It commemorates stampeders of 1897–99.

title: Miles Canyon Bridge — Whitehorse
description: Miles Canyon's basalt cliffs once terrified Klondike stampeders on the Yukon River before a tramway bypassed the rapids. A suspension footbridge now spans quieter water above Schwatka Lake. It sits minutes from downtown Whitehorse.

title: Dempster — Engineer Creek Campground Area
description: Engineer Creek is a classic Dempster Highway stop in continuous wilderness toward the Richardson Mountains. The gravel highway is a modern Indigenous and resource corridor into the Western Arctic. Services are scarce — preparation matters.

title: Inuvik — Our Lady of Victory Igloo Church
description: Inuvik's Igloo Church is a landmark of Canada's Arctic town built for the Mackenzie Delta. The Dempster Highway's end (before the Tuktoyaktuk all-season extension) made Inuvik a pilgrimage for overlanders. Midnight sun and permafrost define life here.

title: Tuktoyaktuk — Pingos and Arctic Ocean Shore
description: Tuktoyaktuk on the Arctic Ocean became reachable by all-season road in 2017, transforming Inuvialuit community access. Pingos — ice-cored hills — are signature landforms. Dipping a toe in the Arctic Ocean is an overlanding rite.

title: Nahanni — Virginia Falls (from park context / Fort Simpson Gateway)
description: Fort Simpson is the primary gateway community for Nahanni National Park Reserve, where Virginia Falls dwarfs Niagara on the South Nahanni River. UNESCO-listed mountain wilderness draws paddlers by floatplane. The Dehcho region is Dene homeland.

title: Elk Island National Park — Astotin Lake Area
description: Elk Island protects plains and wood bison herds in aspen parkland east of Edmonton — a key source for bison restoration projects. Astotin Lake trails offer easy wildlife viewing. It is a conservation success story in miniature.

title: Writing-on-Stone / Áísínai'pi — Visitor Centre Area
description: Áísínai'pi (Writing-on-Stone) holds one of the largest concentrations of Plains Indigenous rock art along the Milk River. Hoodoos and sandstone cliffs form a sacred landscape. UNESCO recognition underscores its cultural importance.

title: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: Head-Smashed-In is a UNESCO buffalo jump used for nearly 6,000 years by Plains peoples to harvest bison. Cliffs and drive lanes remain readable on the land. The interpretive centre is among Canada's finest Indigenous history sites.

title: Prince Albert National Park — Waskesiu Lake
description: Waskesiu is the resort community inside Prince Albert National Park, where Grey Owl once lived and wrote. Boreal lakes and trails sit at the prairie–forest transition. It is central Saskatchewan's signature park gateway.

title: Batoche National Historic Site
description: Batoche was the seat of Louis Riel's Provisional Government and the site of the 1885 Battle of Batoche ending the North-West Resistance. Métis river-lot farms line the South Saskatchewan. It is foundational to Métis nation history.

title: Riding Mountain — Clear Lake Townsite Area
description: Riding Mountain is a forested highland island in a prairie sea, with bison enclosures and Clear Lake recreation. Indigenous and park-creation histories intertwine. Wildlife viewing is excellent along the escarpment.

title: The Forks National Historic Site — Winnipeg
description: The Forks at the Assiniboine and Red rivers has been a meeting place for 6,000 years — Indigenous trade, fur trade, and modern Winnipeg culture. Walkways and markets sit on layered archaeology. It remains the city's gathering heart.

title: Churchill — Cape Merry Battery Area
description: Cape Merry guards the mouth of the Churchill River near Hudson Bay, with forts tied to fur-trade wars. Polar bears stage here in fall waiting for ice. It is one of the most remote iconic wildlife destinations in Canada.

title: Sleeping Giant — Thunder Bay Lookout Area
description: The Sleeping Giant peninsula silhouette defines Thunder Bay's Lake Superior skyline and Anishinaabe legend. Overlooks and Sibley Peninsula trails interpret the formation. Superior's cold inland sea dominates the mood.

title: Pukaskwa — Hattie Cove Trailheads
description: Hattie Cove is the main access to Pukaskwa National Park on Lake Superior's wild northeast shore. Coastal trails follow headlands in Anishinaabe territory. It is Ontario's remote Superior wilderness park.

title: Lake Superior Provincial Park — Old Woman Bay
description: Old Woman Bay's pebble beach sits beneath cliffs said to resemble a face in the rock. The Trans-Canada hugs Superior through this provincial park. Agate hunting and cold swells define the shore.

title: Bruce Peninsula — Grotto / Cyprus Lake Area
description: The Grotto is a wave-cut sea cave in dolostone cliffs of Bruce Peninsula National Park on Georgian Bay. Turquoise water and Niagara Escarpment geology draw heavy visitation. Flowerpot Island's stacks continue the theme offshore.

title: Manitoulin — Cup and Saucer Trailhead Area
description: Cup and Saucer offers Niagara Escarpment cliff views on Manitoulin, the world's largest freshwater island. Anishinaabe cultural presence is strong across the island. Overlooks take in farmland and forest mosaic.

title: Algonquin — Lake of Two Rivers Beach Area
description: Lake of Two Rivers sits on Highway 60 through Algonquin Provincial Park — Ontario's famous canoe-country park founded in 1893. Tom Thomson and the Group of Seven painted these woods. Moose and loons remain icons.

title: Ottawa — Parliament Hill East Block Area
description: Parliament Hill's Gothic Revival buildings house Canada's federal legislature overlooking the Ottawa River. The site was chosen as Queen Victoria's capital for the young Dominion. Changing of the Guard and the Peace Tower define national ritual.

title: Thousand Islands — Rockport / Skydeck Area
description: The Thousand Islands stud the St. Lawrence where ice-sheet flooding drowned a granite landscape. Castles and shipping lanes share the international river. Skydeck views interpret Loyalist and Gilded Age cottage eras.

title: Point Pelee National Park Tip
description: Point Pelee is mainland Canada's southernmost tip and a world-class migratory bird funnel. Marsh boardwalks and a sand tip into Lake Erie define the park. Fall hawk and songbird migrations are legendary.

title: Québec City — Terrasse Dufferin & Château Frontenac
description: Terrasse Dufferin overlooks the St. Lawrence beneath the iconic Château Frontenac in UNESCO Old Québec. French colonial fortifications and Cap Diamant cliffs shape North America's most European cityscape. It is the heart of New France heritage.

title: Charlevoix — Cap-aux-Oies / River Viewpoint Area
description: Charlevoix's half-graben landscape — partly shaped by an ancient impact crater — rolls to the St. Lawrence estuary. Whale-watching waters begin as the river widens. UNESCO biosphere status recognizes the cultural landscape.

title: Saguenay Fjord — Parc national lookout (Baie-Éternité area)
description: The Saguenay Fjord cuts a deep glacial trough into the Canadian Shield with walls over 400 metres. Belugas frequent the St. Lawrence confluence. Baie-Éternité cliffs are among Eastern Canada's most dramatic.

title: Gaspésie — Percé Rock Viewpoint
description: Rocher Percé's pierced limestone stack is the Gaspé Peninsula's icon, changing with tides and rockfalls. Nearby Île Bonaventure hosts a huge gannet colony. It has drawn pilgrims and painters for centuries.

title: Forillon National Park — Cap-Bon-Ami
description: Cap-Bon-Ami's cliffs mark the Appalachians' eastern plunge into the Gulf of St. Lawrence at Forillon. Whale spouts and seabirds share the headland. Expropriation stories of park creation remain part of local memory.

title: Tadoussac — Pointe de l'Islet Whale Lookout
description: Tadoussac sits at the Saguenay–St. Lawrence confluence, a historic Basque whaling and First Nations trade site. Modern whale-watching capital energy fills the bay. Pointe de l'Islet is an easy shore-based lookout.

title: Mauricie — Saint-Maurice River Corridor Lookout
description: La Mauricie National Park protects Laurentian lakes and hills between Montréal and Québec. Former logging country now hosts canoe routes and wolves. Fall color over the Saint-Maurice hills is outstanding.

title: Kouchibouguac — Kellys Beach Boardwalk
description: Kellys Beach boardwalk crosses lagoons to a wide Gulf of St. Lawrence strand in Kouchibouguac National Park. Mi'kmaq homeland and Acadian coastal culture surround the park. Pipewort and shorebirds share the dunes.

title: Fundy National Park — Herring Cove Area
description: Fundy National Park fronts the Bay of Fundy, home to the world's highest tides. Herring Cove and nearby falls show the tidal range's power. Forests behind the shore hide a dense Acadian–Appalachian mosaic.

title: Hopewell Rocks Provincial Park
description: Hopewell Rocks are flowerpot sea stacks you can walk among at low tide and paddle past at high tide. Fundy's tidal range creates the daily transformation. Soft sandstone sculpture is ongoing.

title: Saint John — Reversing Falls Lookout
description: Reversing Falls rapids change direction as Fundy tides overpower the Saint John River outflow. Lookouts interpret one of the Atlantic coast's oddest hydrologic shows. The port city grew around this energy.

title: Confederation Bridge Viewpoint — Cape Jourimain
description: Cape Jourimain looks toward Confederation Bridge, the 13-km link opened in 1997 connecting PEI to the mainland. Marshes around the cape are a national wildlife area. The bridge transformed Island access.

title: Prince Edward Island NP — Green Gables Area
description: Green Gables farmhouse inspired Lucy Maud Montgomery's Anne of Green Gables, drawing literary pilgrims to Cavendish. Dunes and red sandstone cliffs of PEI National Park sit nearby. Potato fields and North Shore beaches define the Island.

title: Cabot Trail — Cap Rouge Lookoff
description: Cap Rouge lookoffs survey French Mountain and coast along one of the world's great scenic drives. The Cabot Trail encircles highland plateaus plunging to the sea. Weather changes fast on exposed headlands.

title: Louisbourg — Fortress National Historic Site
description: The Fortress of Louisbourg is a reconstructed 18th-century French fortified town — once a key North Atlantic stronghold. Sieges of 1745 and 1758 shaped imperial fortunes. Fog and Atlantic swell set the mood.

title: Peggy's Cove Lighthouse
description: Peggy's Cove Light sits on wave-washed granite of St. Margarets Bay, among Canada's most photographed coastal scenes. Fishing village life continues amid tourism. The rocks are beautifully dangerous in swell.

title: Halifax — Citadel National Historic Site
description: Halifax Citadel's star fort has watched the harbor since the mid-1800s, continuing earlier British defenses. Noon gun tradition persists. The hill interprets Halifax's role as an imperial naval town.

title: Kejimkujik National Park Seaside — St. Catherine's River Beach
description: Kejimkujik Seaside protects remote beaches and bog on Nova Scotia's southwest shore, separate from the inland Mi'kmaq canoe park unit. Harbour seals haul out on rocks. It is a quiet Atlantic counterpoint to busier Cabot Trail scenes.

title: Gros Morne — Western Brook Pond Trailhead
description: Western Brook Pond is a landlocked glacial fjord with 600-metre cliffs inside Gros Morne National Park, a UNESCO site showcasing plate tectonics. Boat tours enter after a marsh boardwalk hike. It is Newfoundland's signature inland fjord.

title: Gros Morne — Tablelands Trailhead
description: The Tablelands expose orange peridotite mantle rock — normally deep underground — evidence of the ancient Iapetus Ocean's closure. The barren slopes look like another planet. Gros Morne's geology rewrote Appalachian science.

title: L'Anse aux Meadows National Historic Site
description: L'Anse aux Meadows is the only confirmed Norse site in North America, dating to ~1000 CE. Reconstructed sod buildings interpret Vinland sagas meeting archaeology. It sits at Newfoundland's northern tip on the Strait of Belle Isle.

title: Twillingate — Long Point Lighthouse
description: Long Point Light overlooks Iceberg Alley near Twillingate, where Greenland ice drifts south in spring. Fishing heritage and quiet lanes define Notre Dame Bay towns. Whale spouts often join the bergs.

title: Cape Spear Lighthouse National Historic Site
description: Cape Spear is the easternmost point in North America (excluding Greenland), with a historic light guarding approaches to St. John's. WWII gun batteries share the headland. Sunrise here is among the continent's first.

title: Terra Nova National Park — Newman Sound Area
description: Terra Nova is Newfoundland's first national park, protecting boreal forest meeting sheltered Atlantic reaches. Newman Sound kayak routes explore quiet coves. It is a gentler counterpoint to Gros Morne's drama.

title: Kejimkujik Inland — Merrymakedge Beach Area
description: Inland Kejimkujik protects Mi'kmaq canoe routes, petroglyphs, and loon lakes of southwest Nova Scotia. Merrymakedge is a family beach on Kejimkujik Lake. Cultural interpretation with Mi'kmaq partners is central to the park.

title: Jedediah Smith — Stout Grove Area
description: Stout Grove sits along the Smith River among some of the largest coast redwoods. Ferns and flat alluvial soil grow monumental trees. It is a cathedral of the northern parks complex.

title: Craters rim — Idaho — Menan Buttes Area
description: Menan Buttes are twin tuff cones on the Snake River Plain formed by explosive magma–water interaction. Trails climb the north butte for valley views. They are National Natural Landmarks of basaltic hydrovolcanism.

title: Casper — National Historic Trails Interpretive Center
description: The Trails Center overlooks the North Platte where Oregon, California, Mormon, and Pony Express routes converged. Interactive exhibits simulate river crossings. Casper remains a crossroads of Plains travel.

title: Petrified Forest — Blue Mesa Scenic Road
description: Blue Mesa's bentonite badlands and petrified logs record Late Triassic rivers and conifers turned to quartz. Route 66 and early park history overlap the painted landscape. Crystal-filled wood still dazzles.

title: Saguaro NP East — Broadway Trailhead Area
description: Saguaro National Park's Rincon Mountain district protects classic Sonoran Desert forests of towering saguaros. Broadway access leads into bajada trails at Tucson's edge. Bloom season crowns the giants with white flowers.

title: Great Sand Dunes — Zapata Falls Trailhead
description: Zapata Falls plunges through a narrow slot south of the dunes with Sangre de Cristo views. A short rocky walk reaches the amphitheater. It is a cool counterpoint to hot dune climbs.

title: Pinnacles — High Peaks Trailhead Area
description: Pinnacles protects eroded remnants of an ancient volcano rafted north along the San Andreas. Condors soar over rock spires and talus caves. East and west entrances do not connect by park road.

title: Channel Islands — Ventura Harbor Mainland VC
description: Ventura Harbor is the primary mainland gateway to Channel Islands National Park's Fox Canyon foxes, sea caves, and marine sanctuary waters. Island fox recovery is a conservation win. Crossing the Santa Barbara Channel is the start of the adventure.

title: Red Rock Canyon State Park CA — Scenic Loop
description: Red Rock Canyon's dramatic cliffs along Highway 14 have starred in countless film shoots between Mojave and Walker Pass. Rainbow Basin–style colors meet Joshua trees. It is a quick geologic hit north of Los Angeles routes.

title: Red Rock Canyon NCA — Scenic Drive Entrance
description: Red Rock Canyon's Keystone Thrust landscape rises west of Las Vegas with towering Aztec Sandstone. The 13-mile scenic drive samples pullouts and trailheads. It is a wild contrast to the Strip.

title: Great Basin Highway — Ward Charcoal Ovens
description: Ward Charcoal Ovens' beehive kilns produced charcoal for nearby silver smelters in the 1870s. The stone ovens remain remarkably intact in eastern Nevada. Starry skies here rank among the darkest.

title: Hubbell Trading Post National Historic Site
description: Hubbell Trading Post (1878) still operates on the Navajo Nation as the oldest continuously operating post of its kind in the NPS system. Rugs, jewelry, and cross-cultural trade stories fill the rooms. Ganado's cottonwoods shade the compound.

title: Tonto National Monument Lower Cliff Dwelling
description: Tonto's cliff dwellings overlook Roosevelt Lake in the Superstition foothills, built by Salado peoples. Upper and lower ruins preserve adobe and masonry rooms. The drive via AZ-188 is a Desert Southwest classic.

title: Casa Grande Ruins National Monument
description: Casa Grande's great house is a multi-story Hohokam structure protected by a modern roof since early preservation efforts. Canal irrigation communities thrived in the Gila Valley. It is one of Arizona's oldest federal archaeological preserves.

title: Papohaku Beach Park Molokaʻi
description: One of Hawaiʻi's longest white-sand beaches on Molokaʻi's west shore. Winter surf is often unsafe for swimming. Sunsets feel vast and lonely.

title: Indiana Dunes West Beach
description: Towering Lake Michigan dunes amid steel skylines. Beach-to-oak succession ecology. Chicago skyline on clear days.

title: Starved Rock Lodge IL
description: Sandstone canyons on Illinois River bluffs. CCC lodge. Surprising canyon escape near prairie.

title: Devil's Lake South Shore WI
description: Quartzite bluffs and talus in Baraboo Hills. Glacial blockage made the lake. Wisconsin's busiest state park.

title: Cuyahoga Brandywine Falls
description: Highlight of Cuyahoga Valley NP between Cleveland and Akron. Canal towpath heritage. Urban national park.

title: Seneca Rocks WV
description: Quartzite fin climbing icon above North Fork valley. Observation platform trail. East Coast classic.

title: Letchworth Middle Falls
description: Grand Canyon of the East on the Genesee. Autumn color spectacle. Balloon rallies sometimes fill the sky.

title: Amicalola Falls GA
description: 729-foot cascading falls; Southeast's tallest. AT approach. Blue Ridge foothills lodge views.

title: Cheaha Bald Rock AL
description: Alabama's highest point boardwalk in Talladega NF. CCC park architecture. Piedmont sunrise haze.

title: Avery Island Jungle Gardens
description: Salt dome with Tabasco production and gardens. Bayou surrounds industrial-agricultural oddity. Private island rules.

title: Toadstool Geologic Park NE
description: Badlands and trackways in Oglala National Grassland. Quiet solitude. Flash mud after storms.

title: Ha Ha Tonka Castle Ruins
description: Castle ruins above Lake of the Ozarks on karst. 1900s mansion burned 1942. Springs and sinkholes.

title: Deception Pass Bridge WA
description: Bridge over tidal race named by Vancouver. CCC park surrounds. Notorious currents below.

title: Wapta Falls Yoho
description: Wide Kicking Horse curtain near Yoho west gate. Quieter than Takakkaw. Impressive in runoff.

title: Frank Slide Centre
description: 1903 Turtle Mountain collapse buried Frank in Crowsnest Pass. Canada's deadliest rockslide. Boulders still cover the valley.

title: Horsethief Canyon Drumheller
description: Red Deer River badlands in dinosaur country. Hoodoos and coulees. Royal Tyrrell Museum nearby.

title: Wanuskewin Heritage Park
description: Northern Plains Indigenous cultures along Opimihaw Creek for 6,000+ years. Bison and medicine wheel stories. Living cultural park.
